"四 means ‘four.’ Its present form has enclosing 囗 strokes around inner strokes. One account describes Shang 亖 as four strokes used directly for the numeral; the later graph 四 has disputed origins, including a proposal that it was borrowed for ‘four’ after serving as the original graph of 泗."

"The current graph has enclosing 囗 strokes around inner strokes; this modern description does not establish the ancient identities or roles of those shapes. Ancient analyses remain disputed. One interprets four horizontal marks as counting rods representing four. Another proposes that 四 was a graph for 呬 depicting breath, later reused for ‘four’ because of sound similarity; the depicted referent’s original name is not independently established. A separate proposal treats 四 as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for ‘four’; this proposal lacks textual attestation. Neither borrowing account is established."
"The inner strokes are part of the present graph; their ancient identity and role are unsettled."
